target: यहाँ से स्टेशन सिर्फ़ दो किलोमीटर दूर है।
english: The station is only two kilometers from here.
reason: UNNATURAL/officialese — 'X की दूरी बीस किलोमीटर है' is written-report register; speakers say 'X यहाँ से बीस किलोमीटर दूर है'. Also duplicates hi-0439's distance fact. Replacement keeps the same distance-with-number point in spoken register.

target: पैदल स्टेशन पहुँचने में आधा घंटा लगता है।
english: It takes half an hour to reach the station on foot.
reason: Absurd content — nobody reaches Chennai (a whole city) on foot in half an hour; the sentence is nonsense a learner can never reuse. Same 'में … लगता है' duration structure kept with a believable destination.

target: दरअसल, मुझे थोड़ी ग़लतफ़हमी हो गई थी।
english: Actually, I had a bit of a misunderstanding.
reason: TRANSLATIONESE/officialese — 'पूरी स्थिति के बारे में कोई ग़लतफ़हमी थी' is stiff report language, not speech. Keeps the दरअसल discourse marker and ग़लतफ़हमी in a sentence people actually say.

target: मुझे नई जगहों की तस्वीरें खींचने का बहुत शौक है।
english: I really love taking pictures of new places.
reason: Textbook-essay register — 'प्रकृति की तस्वीरें खींचने का बड़ा शौक' reads like a school 'मेरा शौक' composition. Same शौक + adjective structure, wording people actually use.

target: हमारे घर में सब साथ बैठकर खाना खाते हैं।
english: In our house everyone eats together.
reason: VACUOUS/moralising family motto — 'everyone takes care of each other' says nothing a learner would need to say. Same habitual-present plural pattern with a concrete, usable statement.

target: आज इस दुकान में बीस प्रतिशत की छूट है।
english: Today there's twenty percent off at this shop.
reason: POINTLESS TRIVIA — an exam pass-rate statistic is newsroom filler a learner will never say. Keeps प्रतिशत (percentages) in the everyday shopping context where learners actually meet it.

target: मेरी बेटी ने आज बहुत अच्छी तस्वीर बनाई।
